paper.note: Vesna Marija Potočić Matković, Ivana Salopek Čubrić and Alenka Pavko Čuden (2025), Dependence of Thermal Comfort of Diving Suit on Neoprene Properties and Diving Depth, Polymers 17(21):2820, DOI 10.3390/polym17212820. Tables 1 and 2 with section 2 protocols; 33 study sample groups. CC BY 4.0, copyright 2025 the authors. Attributed numerical facts only; no article text or images redistributed. Table 1 is the numerical authority: M3NOa3 Rct is 0.0535, whereas the narrative gives 0.052. Thermal and thickness/compression test conditions are separately retained; no measured loaded resistance is asserted.

structure.composition_scope: Neoprene identity is reported; whole-assembly polymer, lining, adhesive and additive mass fractions are not reported
structure.identity_scope: Study specimen group from one of four anonymized manufacturers M1-M4; supplier, product, lot and individual coupon identifiers not reported
structure.loading_data_scope: Four measured pressure-specific displacements retained as observations; no loaded thickness, interpolation, unloading, recovery or pressure-invariant Rct inferred
structure.sample_code_scope: NO: no lining; OS: one-sided lining; BS: both-sided linings; final 3, 5 or 7 denotes nominal millimetres. Letter variants remain distinct source groups.
structure.thermal_model_scope: Measured reference dry Rct only. Figures 2 and 4 estimate loaded resistance from cross-sample regression; those estimates are not imported.
